output.reason: [ev-01e97dc9c4df] says that removing the wildcard view permission "may impact reports" as well as mutate and generate policies on custom resources. The proposed exposure only covers mutate/generate policies, so it misses environments exposed through reports, which the reports controller's lost */* get/list/watch permissions confirm [ev-fbb2a078179b, ev-8034700c2e78, ev-2e7e175db33a]. Its undecidable leaf also uses an invalid reason, "environment-visibility-gap". The evidence never says which resources lose visibility, so that part stays undecidable (evidence-gap), joined with Kyverno policies being in use. No overlap is given because [ev-2bbc505de6bb] does not name the Helm values key that restores the wildcard permissions.

correction.statement: Kyverno 1.13 removes the controllers' wildcard view permission and binds them to the default `view` role. Exposed: environments using ClusterPolicy or Policy whose reports, or whose mutate/generate policies, need to view resources (e.g. custom resources) the default view role does not grant. Admission-time policy evaluation is unaffected.

of.needed: which resources (e.g. custom resources) the environment's reports or mutate/generate policies need to view that the default Kubernetes view role does not grant to the Kyverno controllers
